title: The First Fire Emblem Took 30 Years to Leave Japan
hook:
The original Fire Emblem launched on the Famicom in April 1990 and did not get an official English release until December 2020. Then Nintendo pulled it from the eShop after less than four months. Did you grab it before it disappeared?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know the very first Fire Emblem took thirty years to officially leave Japan, and then vanished again after four months? Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light came out on the Famicom in April of nineteen ninety. It was the game that introduced Prince Marth, the hero most Western players first met in Super Smash Brothers. Nintendo never released that cartridge outside Japan. Western players got a DS remake called Shadow Dragon by two thousand nine, but the original stayed home. In October two thousand twenty, Nintendo announced the game was finally getting an English version for the series' thirtieth anniversary. It launched on Switch that December, and it cost less than six dollars. Nintendo added rewind, fast forward, and save states, so the old game was easier to live with. The catch was that the download was only sold until March thirty first, two thousand twenty one, the end of the anniversary. After that it disappeared from the eShop. There was also a forty nine dollar anniversary edition with an NES style box, a replica cartridge, and a hardcover art book. So a game that waited three decades to reach the West was on sale for less than four months. Did you grab it before it vanished? Follow for more gaming history.
